locator: Axiomata, Lex I: Corpus omne perseverare in statu suo quiescendi vel movendi uniformiter in directum, nisi quatenus a viribus impressis cogitur statum illum mutare
interpretation: Every body perseveres in its state of rest or of uniform motion in a straight line, except insofar as impressed forces compel it to change that state; projectiles persevere in their motions except as air resistance and gravity act on them. Read as the rival: some body is being moved (in a respect of uniform motion) while nothing moves it in that respect. Newton calls uniform motion a state (status) and requires impressed force only for a change of state; reading the state as a being moved, and impressed force as the only candidate mover, is the reading this claim takes and the point the Thomist reply contests (DISAMB-MOTION).
